events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 7 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Concede the timing: the rider's 'Can lah, go ahead' at 21:24 (F9) is a rider message sent before the 21:26 segment start (F3) in reply to the driver's 21:23 'Balestier Road' question (F8), so consent to a named road is on the record. That concedes only the existence of consent, not its reach — under RD-5 a named-road authorisation covers travel on that road alone, and nothing in the record ties the driven segment to Balestier Road. [F8 F9 F3] [RD-5]
→ D2: The driver's own brief admits no fact names a road on the driven segment, and F3 gives only a 21:26–21:37 loop of 6.64 km where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, straying up to 2070 m off-route — that is not a description of travel along Balestier Road but of a loop away from the optimal corridor. RD-5 requires a record tying the segment to the agreed road (a stop on it, a locating message, or a road-name fact); absent that, the segment is undetermined on that record (G13), and an undetermined segment that affects the amount goes to a person — the consent cannot be stretched from a named road to 'the corridor' the driver now infers. [F3 F8 F9] [RD-5]
→ D3: The driver's congestion story fails its own test: RD-4(a) needs a traffic incident on the substituted optimal stretch and F15 records none, while F12 is only a speed band (10–19 km/h, 21:06–21:26), which under RD-4(b) is corroboration at most and cannot exempt a segment alone. F14 shows Braddell Road at band 5, but Braddell is a faster road on the driver's chosen loop, not evidence about the optimal route; no fact places slow traffic on the specific stretch of the optimal route that the 21:26–21:37 segment replaced. [F12 F14 F15 F3] [RD-4]
→ D4: The driver's own arithmetic concedes the money: he accepts the billed excess is 5.35 km = $7.54 (F4) and that only the metered distance outside an agreed route is billable, yet the segment he relies on is the 4.89 km of F3 — the 5.35 km billed excess is not attributed by any fact to Balestier Road. I do not contest the $0.11 waiting fee (F5), and the $7.54 the driver offers exceeds the $6.90 my RD-2 computation yields (4.89 km × $1.4098/km from F3 and F7), so his higher figure is a concession against his own interest rather than a defence. [F3 F4 F5 F7] [RD-2 RD-3]
→ D5 (concedes): I agree the claim is capped and ask only $6.90, not the whole fare, so this part is accepted as far as it goes; the driver's clean record (F18) is irrelevant to whether the 4.89 km of F3 is exempt, since RD-6 and profile facts cannot decide route liability and neither party has an upheld route dispute in 90 days (F17, F18). [F7 F18 F17] [RD-2 RD-6]
→ D6 (concedes): No safety escalation is sought from this side either; the record contains only the route exchange (F8, F9, F10) plus the driver's post-trip statement (F11), and F15/F16 show no incident and fair weather, so SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 are not engaged and the case can be decided on the route facts.
